newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks race up while Wall Street falls.
newsitem.headline: French stocks race up while Wall Street falls.

text.p: French shares closed markedly higher despite a fall on Wall Street, pushed by fresh liquidity and corporate as well as economic forecasts.
"It's the de-coupling!," a French broker cheered, using the term for Europe going its own way and ignoring Wall Street. U.S. investors were buying European shares.
The New York market continued its decline on Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's Wednesday warning and on higher than expected rise in January durable goods orders.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed up 27.23 points or 1.05 percent at 2,629.40.
"This rise is rather extraordinary," another broker said, without being able to identify a reason for the rise.
"People are still ready to buy on Wall Street," he added.
On Friday, the French blue-chip index is expected to try and break its all-time record, set on February 18, of 2,658.62.

German shares were also rising strongly with bunds on hopes for a German tax reform agreement. Italy's Prime Minister Romano Prodi said he would not ask for a delay of European monetary union or easy terms to join the single currency.
* Volume was 7.7 billion francs of which 6.2 billion in CAC-40 stocks.
* Renault closed up nearly five percent at 130 francs. The company said it expected 1996 losses to be "significant," in a statement saying it would stop making cars in Belgium.
On Wednesday the French government declined to participate in an early retirement scheme which Renault and PSA had proposed to help them reduce their costs.
"They have to tackle it themselves now," a broker said.
* Peugeot closed 2.44 percent up at 587 francs.
* Sanofi closed up 3.54 percent at 555 francs on market talk of alliances and a technical catching up, dealers said.

Jean-Francois Dehecq, chairman of the Elf Aquitaine majority controlled company, on Wednesday indicated that the company could seek a number of alliances and mergers, both in Europe and the United States. "There is a lot of alliance talk in the market following the declarations by Dehecq," a dealer said.
A London-based broker added that the Sanofi share had underperformed the market in the past few days following its 1996 results on Tuesday, and was now catching up.
* AGF was most actively traded stock and lost 4.84 percent to 208.90 francs as a recent run on takeover speculation ran out of steam.
* Danone closed 2.67 percent higher, also boosted by takeover rumours naming Unilever UNLV.L as possible buyers. Analysts said such a move would not make sense for Unilever.
Other rumours were that Italy's IFIL may want to raise its stake in Danone to add to its food portfolio, in which it has a 20 percent stake in the newly formed Worms and Saint-Louis combination.
* GAN and UIC were suspended on Thursday and are expected to requote on Friday. Finance Minister Jean Arthuis is giving a news conference this afternoon on GAN.
The French government is expected to reveal rescue plans for the loss-making, state-controlled insurance Groupe des Assurances Nationale (GAN), which could hit 20 billion francs.
Some 20 percent of GAN is listed.
* Thomson-CSF closed 1.1 percent lower at 180.50 francs. The government published a privatisation decree for its 58-percent stake in the defence electronics group today.
-- Marcel Michelson, Paris newsroom +33 1 4221 5452
